title: 「退避勧告」からわずか1時間半の為替介入　連休前の市場に衝撃
extracted_text: 政府・日銀が円安食い止めのため、約1年9カ月ぶりに円買い・ドル売り介入に踏み切った。事前に介入実行を強く示唆する異例の手法で、大型連休前の市場に衝撃が走った。何が起きたのか。 「いよいよ断固たる措置を取るタイミングが近づいている」。外国為替市場で円相場が1ドル＝160円台半ばをつけた4月30日夕、片山さつき財務相と財務省の三村淳財務官が報道陣の前でそれぞれ発言し、為替介入に踏み切る考えを示唆した。これに加えて三村氏は「最後の退避勧告だ」とまで述べ、介入の本気度を疑う市場に「最後通告」を突きつけた。 三村氏の発言から1時間半後の30日午後7時過ぎ、外国為替市場で円は突然急騰し、1時間以上かけ、155円台半ばまで円高に振れた。発言前からの変動幅は約5円で、市場では「介入としか考えられない」（大手行幹部）との見方が広がった。 三村氏は5月1日、記者団の質問に対し、介入したかどうか明言を避けた。だが政府関係者は非公式に介入を実施したことを認めた。
translated_text:
The government and Bank of Japan took the rare step of buying yen and selling dollars for the first time in about 1 year and 9 months to stem the yen's depreciation. The unusual approach of strongly hinting at intervention beforehand sent shockwaves through the market just before the long holiday. What happened?

"The time for decisive action is approaching." On the evening of April 30th, when the yen was trading around the mid-160s against the dollar in the foreign exchange market, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and Vice Finance Minister Jun Mimura each spoke to the press, hinting at their intention to intervene in the market. On top of this, Mimura went so far as to call it "the final withdrawal warning," delivering an "ultimatum" to a market that doubted the government's resolve to actually intervene.

Just 1 hour and 35 minutes after Mimura's statement, after 7 p.m. on the 30th, the yen suddenly surged in the foreign exchange market, taking more than an hour to appreciate to the mid-155s. The price movement was about 5 yen from before the statement, leading markets to spread the view that "it can only be seen as intervention" according to a major bank official.

On May 1st, Mimura dodged questions from reporters about whether intervention had been carried out. However, a government source informally confirmed that the intervention had taken place.
title_en: FX Intervention Just 1½ Hours After 'Withdrawal Warning' Shocks Market Before Holiday
